title_o: Perceiving Aggression from Facial Structure: Further Evidence for A Positive Association with Facial Width–To–Height Ratio and Masculinity, but Not for Moderation by Self–Reported Dominance

replications.quote: participants choosing the higher facial width-to-height ratio (fWHR) face as more aggressive in 58.3% of the trials. This was significantly above chance [t(101) = 4.06, p < .001]

The one-sample t-test conducted found the meanchance of choosing the higher fWHR as the more aggressive (53.96%) was significantly greater than 50%[t(287) = 2.99, p = .003, Cohen’s d = .18]. Thus, this replication of the claim was successful according to the SCORE criteria.
